generatedCommentsNodes.comment: Replacing `entrySet().forEach(x -> …)` with `map.forEach((k, v) -> …)` is a clean simplification. No issues.

`functionName(Class)` performs a linear scan over `defs.values()` on every call. This is invoked from `PlanningMetrics.function(Class)` (`#PS068`), which in turn is called from `ExpressionBuilder.castToType` (`#36E4Q`) for **every** cast expression in the query. With a large function registry and many casts, this becomes O(casts × functions). Consider maintaining a reverse `Map<Class, String>` alongside `defs` for O(1) lookup.
Using `map.compute(key, (k, count) -> …)` instead of `get` + `put` is a good improvement (single atomic operation on the map). No issues.
The `MetricsAware` interface and its default `metricName()` are clean. The Javadoc has a minor typo ("overwriten" → "overwritten"), but that's cosmetic.

`PlanningMetrics.command()` throws a `QlIllegalArgumentException` when `metricName()` returns `null`. The `MetricsAware` default never returns null, but `UnresolvedRelation.metricName()` (`#DMX0F`) delegates to the `commandName` field, which is explicitly set to `null` in `#ENYZX` (METRICS relation) and `#CG8GE` (JOIN relation) to opt out of counting. If such a node ever reaches `command()`, the query will fail with an exception rather than simply being skipped. Since the intent of setting `commandName` to `null` is "don't count this," a `null` guard that silently returns (or checks before calling `command()`) would be more robust than throwing.

The new cast/alias test case and the removal of `"FROM TS"` / `"STATS"` from the METRICS and INLINESTATS expectations are consistent with the implementation changes (`#ENYZX`, `#K3KBN`, `#2DD88`). No issues here.

Removing the abstract `commandName()` from `LogicalPlan` is the right move; it eliminates the need for every plan node (including non-user-facing ones like `TopN`, `EsRelation`, `StubRelation`, `LocalRelation`) to provide a name. The corresponding removals in `#N2B58`, `#TH3RH`, `#7VZT5`, `#FVBFD`, `#DPHR3`, `#0FHTQ`, `#XWQSH` are all consistent.

Renaming `plan.commandName()` → `plan.metricName()` in `Analyzer.ResolveTable#resolveIndex` is consistent with the interface migration. These call sites presumably operate on `UnresolvedRelation` (which implements `MetricsAware`), so the call resolves correctly.
